title: tokenizer-aware-regex-backend: stabilize streaming constrained decoding and OpenAI-compat behavior
author: Ava Patel
description:
Motivation:
Streaming constrained decoding (CFG / regex backends) has repeatedly hit edge-cases when token boundaries split grammar tokens or regex groups across byte/utf boundaries. These issues manifested as: truncated JSON outputs during streaming, invalid function-calling payloads when tool arguments contained emoji or non-BMP characters, and mismatches between the OpenAI-compat layer's incremental transcript and the runtime's internal tokenization state.

This PR implements a tokenizer-aware regex/grammar constrained-decoding backend that: 1) tracks token boundary alignment between the tokenizer and the constrained automaton, 2) defers constraint acceptance until a full tokenizer-aligned unit is available (so streaming partial tokens don't prematurely satisfy regex groups), and 3) exposes a deterministic fallback policy for cases where a constraint would otherwise block progress (configurable to emit escape tokens, apply best-effort repair, or route to a fallback model variant).

What changed (high level):
- Add TokenBoundaryAdapter: a small shim that normalizes tokenizer tokenization events (including multi-codepoint grapheme clusters, surrogate pairs, and byte-encoded tokens) into canonical "token spans" used by constrained backends.
- Regex backend update: convert the streaming regex matcher to operate on token-span sequences rather than raw bytes/characters. This prevents false-positive group matches when a regex group crosses a tokenizer split.
- CFG backend adjustment: similar token-aligned acceptance checks added to avoid accepting a parse on partial token streams.
- OpenAI-compat streaming bridge: ensure delta messages emitted to clients reflect token-aligned content and include explicit "partial_token" flags when the client wants the in-flight bytes (opt-in). By default we keep the previous behavior but correct ordering so that client-visible incremental JSON tokens are valid JSON fragments.
- Function-calling fixes: ensure tool arguments reconstructed from streaming fragments preserve high-level token boundaries. Add tests covering emoji and non-Latin scripts in tool args.
- New tests: unit + fuzz harness for token boundary + regex interactions, integration test for streaming OpenAI-compat outputs, and canary tests that run a constrained-decoder workload against the internal perf canary cluster.
- Docs: document new config knobs (constraint_fallback: [escape|repair|fallback_model], streaming_partial_tokens: [true|false]) and guidance on selecting policies for low-latency vs correctness tradeoffs.

"Structured output: introduce tokenizer-aware constrained decoding backend. Fixes several streaming correctness bugs where tokenization boundaries (emoji, multi-codepoint glyphs, and non-ASCII scripts) could cause malformed JSON or incorrect function-calling payloads during streaming. Adds a configurable fallback policy for stalled constraints and an opt-in partial_token streaming flag. Backward compatible by default; see docs for migration steps."
